oneLine: Grades each fulfillment node on what it actually did over the last 7 and 30 days, and tells the network when a grade changes.

rows.title: Remember a purchase order's deadlines
rows.story: When a vendor is sent a purchase order, this context keeps its ship-by and acknowledge-by deadlines. Later facts are judged against them. Nothing is counted yet.
rows.policy: Whenever a purchase order is issued, keep its ship-by and acknowledge-by deadlines

rows.title: Fill in the ship-by deadline
rows.story: The shipment confirmation repeats the ship-by deadline. It is merged into what is already known, so either message can arrive first. The vendor's own ship time is not used.
rows.policy: Whenever a vendor confirms a shipment, complete the purchase order's ship-by deadline

rows.title: Judge an acknowledgement
rows.story: A vendor accepts or rejects a purchase order. The answer counts as late if it comes in the last tenth of the time allowed. Without the order's deadlines it cannot be judged and is retried.
rows.policy: Whenever a purchase order is accepted or rejected, record how timely the answer was

rows.title: Count an expired order
rows.story: A purchase order ran out of time without an answer. That counts against the node as a late acknowledgement, always.
rows.policy: Whenever a purchase order expires, record a late acknowledgement

rows.title: Judge a handover against the ship-by time
rows.story: The carrier took a package from the node. It counts as on time if the handover is not after the purchase order's ship-by time; the exact boundary is on time.
rows.policy: Whenever a package is handed over, record whether it beat the ship-by time

rows.title: Count a kept promise
rows.story: delivery-promise says a delivery promise was kept. That counts in the node's favour.
rows.policy: Whenever a promise is kept, record it for the node

rows.title: Count a broken promise, if it is the node's fault
rows.story: A broken promise only counts against the node when the cause is the node's: late, late handover, vendor refusal or an unanswered order. A lost or returned package is the network's, and is ignored.
rows.policy: Whenever a promise is broken, record it only for a cause the node is responsible for

rows.title: Count an inventory feed
rows.story: offer-availability applied a stock feed from the node. The gaps between feeds show how fresh the node's stock numbers are.
rows.policy: Whenever a node's inventory feed is applied, record the time of the feed

rows.title: Note when an inbound shipment left
rows.story: A seller's shipment to the node has been shipped. Its ship time is kept, first one wins, to compare with the receipt later. It is shown on reads but never graded.
rows.policy: Whenever an inbound shipment is shipped, keep its shipped time

rows.title: Note what an inbound receipt found
rows.story: The node reports what it received for a shipment. Carton counts are kept, the first report wins, and the receipt is joined to the shipment when both are known. Shown on reads, never graded.
rows.policy: Whenever an inbound receipt is submitted, keep its carton counts

rows.title: Note the node's declared profile and do nothing
rows.story: The node's declared profile arrives and is only logged as seen. A grade comes from observed facts, never from what a vendor declared.
rows.policy: Whenever a node declares its profile, record that the message arrived and change nothing

rows.title: Recompute the grades
rows.story: A periodic run recomputes every scorecard that has new facts or facts that left the window. A node needs 50 observations to get an A to D grade; below that it stays provisional and nothing is published.
rows.policy: Every run, recompute the due scorecards and announce a changed grade or metric

then.does: keeps the 30-day grade; B pads handling time, C and D skip a pickup option
keeps the 30-day grade and adds a cost penalty for B, C and D

rows.title: Warn when a metric gets worse
rows.story: When a graded node's metric crosses its bound in the wrong direction between two graded runs, a breach is raised, one per metric. It goes to analytics only, nobody in the network reacts.
rows.policy: Whenever a graded scorecard changes, raise a breach for each metric that crossed its bound

rows.title: Suspend or reinstate a node's fast tiers
rows.story: On the 7-day card, a graded on-time handover rate below 90% suspends the node from same-day and next-day. Three separate days at 95% or better reinstate it. Each flip is announced once per tier.
rows.policy: Every run, flip a node's fast-tier eligibility when its 7-day on-time rate says so

then.does: keeps each node's eligibility per tier and leaves ineligible nodes out of fast-tier offers

hotspots.text: A handover or answer that beats its purchase order is retried, then parked in a failure queue. Nothing re-processes that queue.
Declared profile next to measured behaviour is not modelled: the profile message is received and ignored.
The broken-promise causes the model names differ from what delivery-promise sends; in practice only LATE counts against a node.
Inbound accuracy mixes node and seller causes until they are separated. It is informational and never graded.
After a stuck event hits its send-attempt cap, a later event of the same scorecard can reach consumers first.

opportunities.text: If inbound timeliness should count towards a grade, a new decision is needed: the facts would become observations.
A node directory or a declared-versus-measured view could use the profile messages already received.
A compacted counter form is the follow-up if one node's volume grows by orders of magnitude.
